title: Follow any playback end to end, and see why the cluster needed more workers
description: Serves "Nothing is hidden.". An operator must be able to see exactly where a playback stalled and why the cluster needed more workers, not only that a film is transcoding. Metrics (JS-019) give totals: stalls happened, the queue is deep. This adds one OpenTelemetry trace per playback (PlaySessionId) across the api, stream and worker processes: PlaybackInfo and its decision with reasons; each segment request and where its time went (served from the store, waited on a job, started a job); the job queued, claimed (queue time, which worker) and its ffmpeg runs with their speed; helpers started, and helpers wanted but not started for lack of a free slot; and a failover (lock lost, reap, replacement). The reasons for more workers become metrics too, which autoscaling (JS-057) scales on, so the reason it scaled is visible. Viewers keep seeing in their app that a film is transcoding and why (JS-067).
acceptanceCriteria: One trace per playback session spans the api, stream and worker processes, its context carried in the transcode job row across the Postgres handoff

Given a stalled segment (over 5 s), its trace shows which part took the time: waiting for a free slot, an encode slower than real time, the upload, or reading the store; the stall metric links to the trace (exemplar)
A failover shows the dead worker's span end and the replacement's begin in one trace
Helper decisions are traced and counted: helpers started with the job's speed, and helpers wanted but not started because no slot was free
The demand number and its reasons are JS-164's; a playback's trace shows the same reason for that playback, so why the cluster grew can be read back from either
Log lines carry the trace id, so a trace leads to its logs
Exported over OTLP to any backend, off by default; the dogfood runs a backend and the docs show reading a stall from it
Checked with real processes: a test collector receives a playback's trace from three processes, with a stall and a failover in it
Each request and job log line carries ids that link them
notes: Needs a design review; the homelab has no tracing backend yet (Tempo suggested). Product owner (2026-11-08): wants to trace everything through the pipeline, see where something stalled and why more workers were needed; placed before P6 (Kubernetes). JS-024 review (UX): Sessions can show the viewer's job as done while helpers encode, and no log line says a helper started. Takes in the logging slice (formerly JS-022): its log-line criterion. The product owner cut JS-022 as a duplicate on 2026-11-27.
